17178-westerfelt.title: A Novel
17178-westerfelt.creator: Will N. Harben
17178-westerfelt.description: A book by Will N. Harben. Others affirmed that her sister was slowly nagging the life out of her, and simply because she had been blessed with that which had been denied her--a daughter. Be this as it may, everybody who knew Mrs. Slogan knew that she never lost an opportunity to find fault with the girl, who was considered quite pretty and had really a gentle, lovable disposition.

26750-memorial-address-on-the-life-and-c.creator: Unknown
26750-memorial-address-on-the-life-and-c.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In the fulness of time a republic rose up in the wilderness of America. Thousands of years had passed away before this child of the ages could be born. From whatever there was of good in the systems of former centuries she drew her nourishment; the wrecks of the past were her warnings. With the deepest sentiment of faith fixed in her inmost nature, she disenthralled religion from bondage to temporal power, that her worship might be worship only in spirit and in truth.

arxiv-2106-00487.title: Dense Nested Attention Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
arxiv-2106-00487.creator: Boyang Li, Chao Xiao, Longguang Wang, Yingqian Wang, Zaiping Lin, Miao Li, Wei An, Yulan Guo
arxiv-2106-00487.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Boyang Li, Chao Xiao, Longguang Wang, Yingqian Wang, Zaiping Lin, Miao Li, Wei An, Yulan Guo. Single-frame infrared small target (SIRST) detection aims at separating small targets from clutter backgrounds. With the advances of deep learning, CNN-based methods have yielded promising results in generic object detection due to their powerful modeling capability. However, existing CNN-based methods cannot be directly applied to infrared small targets since pooling layers in their networks could lead to the loss of targets in deep layers.

arxiv-2407-18675.title: A dual ensemble classifier used to recognise contaminated multi-channel EMG and MMG signals in the control of upper limb bioprosthesis
arxiv-2407-18675.creator: Pawel Trajdos, Marek Kurzynski
arxiv-2407-18675.description: Abstract Myopotential pattern recognition to decode the intent of the user is the most advanced approach to controlling a powered bioprosthesis. Unfortunately, many factors make this a difficult problem and achieving acceptable recognition quality in real-word conditions is a serious challenge.

arxiv-2409-05158.title: Derived equivalences for the derived discrete algebras are standard
arxiv-2409-05158.creator: Grzegorz Bobiński, Tomasz Ciborski
arxiv-2409-05158.description: Abstract . We prove that any derived equivalence between derived discrete algebras is standard, i.e. is isomorphic to the derived tensor product by a two-sided tilting complex. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 18E30; Secondary: 16G10 † † Corresponding Author . arxiv-2409-19696.title: Vision-Language Models are Strong Noisy Label Detectors
arxiv-2409-19696.creator: Tong Wei, Hao-Tian Li, Chun-Shu Li, Jiang-Xin Shi, Yu-Feng Li, Min-Ling Zhang
arxiv-2409-19696.description: Abstract Recent research on fine-tuning vision-language models has demonstrated impressive performance in various downstream tasks. However, the challenge of obtaining accurately labeled data in real-world applications poses a significant obstacle during the fine-tuning process. To address this challenge, this paper presents a De noising F ine- T uning framework, called DeFT , for adapting vision-language models.

arxiv-2505-03096.title: Assessing and Enhancing the Robustness of LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems Through Chaos Engineering
arxiv-2505-03096.creator: Joshua Owotogbe
arxiv-2505-03096.description: Abstract This study explores the application of chaos engineering to enhance the robustness of Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MAS) in production-like environments under real-world conditions. LLM-MAS can potentially improve a wide range of tasks, from answering questions and generating content to automating customer support and improving decision-making processes.

arxiv-2506-02944.title: Interior of a black hole in the framework of the scalar quasiparticle model
arxiv-2506-02944.creator: S. Bondarenko, D. Cheskis, R. Singh
arxiv-2506-02944.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. Bondarenko, D. Cheskis, R. Singh. We have developed an effective thermodynamic model for a black hole’s interior composed of scalar quasiparticles. The proposed interior consists of a core and a crust; the properties of both depend on the kinetics of the quasiparticles. In the core, the quasiparticles possess zero classical kinetic energy; the total potential energy U ⁡ ( N ) U(N) of the core depends only on the number N N of quasiparticles inside it.

arxiv-2512-03038.title: A new constraint on the y y -distortion with FIRAS: implications for feedback models in galaxy formation and cosmic shear measurements
arxiv-2512-03038.creator: Giulio Fabbian, Federico Bianchini, Alina Sabyr, J. Colin Hill, Christopher C. Lovell, Leander Thiele, David N. Spergel
arxiv-2512-03038.description: Abstract The y y -type distortion of the blackbody spectrum of the cosmic microwave background radiation probes the pressure of the gas trapped in galaxy groups and clusters. We reanalyze archival data of the FIRAS instrument with an improved astrophysical foreground cleaning technique, and measure a mean y y -distortion of ⟨ y ⟩ = ( 1.2 ± 2.

arxiv-2512-22255.title: Shape of Thought: When Distribution Matters More than Correctness in Reasoning Tasks
arxiv-2512-22255.creator: Abhranil Chandra, Ayush Agrawal, Arian Hosseini, Sebastian Fischmeister, Rishabh Agarwal, Navin Goyal, Aaron Courville
arxiv-2512-22255.description: Abstract We present the surprising finding that a language model’s reasoning capabilities can be improved by training on synthetic datasets of chain-of-thought (CoT) traces from more capable models, even when all of those traces lead to an incorrect final answer. Our experiments show this approach can yield better performance on reasoning tasks than training on human-annotated datasets.

arxiv-2601-01813.title: Spatio-temporal modeling and forecasting with Fourier neural operators
arxiv-2601-01813.creator: Pratik Nag, Andrew Zammit-Mangion, Sumeetpal Singh, Noel Cressie
arxiv-2601-01813.description: Abstract Spatio-temporal process models are often used for modeling dynamic physical and biological phenomena that evolve across space and time. These phenomena may exhibit environmental heterogeneity and complex interactions that are difficult to capture using traditional statistical process models such as Gaussian processes.

pmc-12562885.title: Genetic and Functional Characterization of STAT4 in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients with Distinct Disease Activity
pmc-12562885.creator: Karla Mayela Bravo-Villagra, Rocio Guadalupe Hernández-Ruíz, Alejandra Landeros-Sáenz, Christian Johana Baños-Hernández, Sergio Cerpa-Cruz, Samuel García-Arellano, José Francisco Muñoz-Valle, Andres López-Quintero, Julian Ramírez-Bello
pmc-12562885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by chronic inflammation mediated by the JAK/STAT pathway. Variants in STAT4 have been associated with autoimmune susceptibility, but their functional role in RA remains unclear. The aim of this study was to genetically and functionally characterize STAT4 in RA patients with varying disease activity by analyzing two variants, mRNA expression, phosphorylated STAT4 (pSTAT4), and inflammatory cytokines (IL-12, IL-23, and IFN-γ). Sixty-three Mexican patients with RA were stratified into remission/low and moderate/high activity groups.

pmc-12672957.creator: Abdalftah Noureldin Abdalftah Osman, Basil Hamed, Mohammed Ali Mohammed Ali, Aboaagla Abdalbagi Ali Awad Alkareem, Fatima Essamaldin Altahir Mohamed Alsharif, Ammar Abdelrahman Hussein Dousa, Abdelmuniem Siddig Mohamed Ahmed, Malaz Siddeg Younis, Elkhatab Abdulrahman Mustafa Abdulrahman, Mohammed Os
pmc-12672957.description: BackgroundCommunication failure at the point of handoff is one of the most significant preventable medical errors, especially in resource-scarce settings. Worldwide, the use of the I-PASS (Illness severity, Patient summary, Action list, Situation awareness and contingency planning, and Synthesis by receiver) tool has been shown to improve the accuracy and consistency of handovers of patients.

pmc-13490536.title: A murine proof-of-concept study of polatuzumab vedotin in combination with venetoclax in experimental therapy of BCL2-positive aggressive lymphomas
pmc-13490536.creator: Eva Pokorna, Dmitry Manakov, Kristyna Nozickova, Petra Kovarikova, Alexandra Dolnikova, Nicol Renesova, Liliana Tuskova, Magdalena Klanova, Zuzana Vreckova, Ondrej Havranek, Marek Trneny, Pavel Klener
pmc-13490536.description: We evaluated the in vivo efficacy of polatuzumab vedotin (POLA), administered as a single agent or in combination with venetoclax (VEN), in relapsed/refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) and BCL2-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). In addition, we investigated the mechanisms underlying acquired resistance to POLA in vivo.

pmc-13550603.title: Olverembatinib, a novel BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor, exhibits anti-tumor activity and synergizes with gemcitabine in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
pmc-13550603.creator: Zengfei Xia, Runduan Lin, Fan Luo, Qiuyun Luo, Jing Yang, Shan Shi, Yan Li, Jiaxing Cao, Miaozhen Qiu, Lin Zhang, Wenlong Guan, Dajun Yang
pmc-13550603.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal diseases with few treatment options. The aberrant activation of SRC PDAC suggests it as a promising therapeutic target. Here, we evaluated the antitumor activity of olverembatinib, a novel multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor, as a single agent and in combination with gemcitabine, the standard chemotherapeutic backbone for PDAC treatment.
